fruits.extendedStory: In 1790 Giovanni Battista Guglielmini climbed to the top with a ball of lead. He let it go and watched where it landed. It did not fall straight down, but drifted a little to the east. That small drift was his evidence that the Earth is turning under us. The tower carries the name of the Asinelli, and a document of 1185 already knew it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: 1790 stieg Giovanni Battista Guglielmini mit einer Bleikugel bis nach oben. Er ließ sie los und schaute, wo sie aufkam. Sie fiel nicht gerade nach unten, sondern wich ein wenig nach Osten ab. Diese kleine Abweichung war sein Beleg dafür, dass sich die Erde unter uns dreht. Der Turm trägt den Namen der Asinelli, und schon eine Urkunde von 1185 kannte ihn.
localizedExtendedStory.en: In 1790 Giovanni Battista Guglielmini climbed to the top with a ball of lead. He let it go and watched where it landed. It did not fall straight down, but drifted a little to the east. That small drift was his evidence that the Earth is turning under us. The tower carries the name of the Asinelli, and a document of 1185 already knew it.

localizedStory.de: In diesem schiefen Backsteinturm winden sich 498 Stufen fast 97 Meter empor. Seit 1150 steht er über der Strada Maggiore.
localizedStory.en: Inside this leaning brick tower, 498 steps wind nearly 97 metres up. It has stood over Strada Maggiore since 1150.

fruits.name: Asinelli
fruits.story: Inside this leaning brick tower, 498 steps wind nearly 97 metres up. It has stood over Strada Maggiore since 1150.

fruits.extendedStory: The square measures 115 metres by 60, which is room enough for a crowd. Its middle is a little higher than the rest, a rectangle of white and pink granite laid in 1934. It stands 15 centimetres above the paving. Bologna calls it the crescentone, after the crescente, a salted flatbread from its own kitchens.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Platz misst 115 mal 60 Meter und ist damit weit. Seine Mitte liegt ein wenig höher, ein Rechteck aus weißem und rosa Granit, verlegt 1934. Es ragt 15 Zentimeter über das Pflaster. Bologna nennt es crescentone, nach der crescente, einem salzigen Fladenbrot aus der eigenen Küche.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The square measures 115 metres by 60, which is room enough for a crowd. Its middle is a little higher than the rest, a rectangle of white and pink granite laid in 1934. It stands 15 centimetres above the paving. Bologna calls it the crescentone, after the crescente, a salted flatbread from its own kitchens.

localizedStory.de: Bolognas großer Treffpunkt seit 1550. Alte Paläste umringen ihn, und gleich daneben plätschert der Neptunbrunnen.
localizedStory.en: Bologna's great meeting place since 1550. Grand old palaces ring it, and Neptune's Fountain splashes just beside.

fruits.name: Piazza Maggiore
fruits.story: Bologna's great meeting place since 1550. Grand old palaces ring it, and Neptune's Fountain splashes just beside.

fruits.extendedStory: Arturo Carpi drew this hall, and an engineer called Luigi Mellucci worked on it with him. What moved in under the roof were the treccole, the old food stalls of Bologna. They had traded out in the open on Piazza Maggiore, and they came here for good. The market opened its doors again in 1949, and the stalls have kept going ever since. A piece of the big square has been living indoors ever since.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Arturo Carpi entwarf die Halle, gemeinsam mit dem Ingenieur Luigi Mellucci. Unter das Dach zogen die treccole ein, Bolognas alte Lebensmittelstände. Sie hatten unter freiem Himmel auf der Piazza Maggiore gestanden und kamen für immer hierher. 1949 öffnete der Markt wieder, und die Stände halten seither durch. Ein Stück des großen Platzes wohnt seitdem im Haus.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Arturo Carpi drew this hall, and an engineer called Luigi Mellucci worked on it with him. What moved in under the roof were the treccole, the old food stalls of Bologna. They had traded out in the open on Piazza Maggiore, and they came here for good. The market opened its doors again in 1949, and the stalls have kept going ever since. A piece of the big square has been living indoors ever since.

localizedStory.de: Unter diesem Dach verkauft Bologna sein Gemüse und frische Lebensmittel. Die Halle wurde 1910 entworfen, an der Via San Gervasio.
localizedStory.en: Under this roof Bologna sells its greens and fresh food. The hall was drawn up in 1910, off Via San Gervasio.

fruits.name: Mercato delle Erbe
fruits.story: Under this roof Bologna sells its greens and fresh food. The hall was drawn up in 1910, off Via San Gervasio.

fruits.extendedStory: Carlo Francesco Dotti drew the building. Work started in 1712, but the doors did not open to readers until 1756. That is forty-four years between the laying of the stone and the reading of the books. The shelves sit in the university quarter, where students have walked for centuries.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Carlo Francesco Dotti entwarf das Gebäude für die Universität. Der Bau begann 1712, doch erst 1756 durften Leser hinein. Zwischen Baubeginn und den Lesern lagen vierundvierzig Jahre. Die Regale stehen im Universitätsviertel an der Via Zamboni, wo seit Jahrhunderten Studenten unterwegs sind.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Carlo Francesco Dotti drew the building. Work started in 1712, but the doors did not open to readers until 1756. That is forty-four years between the laying of the stone and the reading of the books. The shelves sit in the university quarter, where students have walked for centuries.

localizedStory.de: Die Universitätsbibliothek Bolognas an der Via Zamboni. 1712 begonnen, 1756 für Leser geöffnet.
localizedStory.en: Bologna's university library on Via Zamboni. Begun in 1712 and opened to readers in 1756.

fruits.name: Biblioteca Universitaria
fruits.story: Bologna's university library on Via Zamboni. Begun in 1712 and opened to readers in 1756.

fruits.extendedStory: Before you go in, step under the covered walkway that runs along its side. That portico is credited to Antonio di Vincenzo, around 1392. The church itself had grown by then, made bigger in 1383 by Andrea da Faenza. Inside hangs a painted panel of the Maestà by Cimabue, from about 1285. It is older than the church that holds it.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Geh hinein, aber schau vorher unter den überdachten Gang an ihrer Seite. Dieser Portikus wird Antonio di Vincenzo zugeschrieben, um 1392. Die Kirche selbst war da schon gewachsen: 1383 vergrößerte sie Andrea da Faenza. Drinnen hängt eine Maestà-Tafel von Cimabue, von etwa 1285. Sie ist älter als die Kirche, die sie beherbergt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Before you go in, step under the covered walkway that runs along its side. That portico is credited to Antonio di Vincenzo, around 1392. The church itself had grown by then, made bigger in 1383 by Andrea da Faenza. Inside hangs a painted panel of the Maestà by Cimabue, from about 1285. It is older than the church that holds it.

localizedStory.de: Eine Kirche von 1345 an der Strada Maggiore, nahe der alten Basilika Santo Stefano.
localizedStory.en: A church begun in 1345, standing on Strada Maggiore near the old Santo Stefano basilica.

fruits.name: Santa Maria dei Servi
fruits.story: A church begun in 1345, standing on Strada Maggiore near the old Santo Stefano basilica.

fruits.extendedStory: The name is not decoration: this theatre began its life with no roof at all. It was the house given over to daytime shows, so the plays ran by sunlight. Carlo Aspari drew it, and Pietro Bonini had it built. The benches filled with workers, cigar-makers, laundresses and porters. They sat more equally here than in the old theatres of private boxes.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Name ist keine Zierde: Dieses Theater begann ganz ohne Dach. Es war das Haus für die Vorstellungen am Tag, gespielt wurde also im Sonnenlicht. Carlo Aspari entwarf es, und Pietro Bonini ließ es bauen. Auf den Bänken saßen Arbeiter, Zigarrenmacherinnen, Wäscherinnen und Träger. Sie saßen hier gleicher als in den alten Theatern mit ihren Logen.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The name is not decoration: this theatre began its life with no roof at all. It was the house given over to daytime shows, so the plays ran by sunlight. Carlo Aspari drew it, and Pietro Bonini had it built. The benches filled with workers, cigar-makers, laundresses and porters. They sat more equally here than in the old theatres of private boxes.

localizedStory.de: Teatro Arena del Sole heißt 'Arena der Sonne'. Es wurde 1810 als Theater eröffnet, an der kleinen Piazzetta Dino Sarti.
localizedStory.en: The Arena del Sole means the 'Arena of the Sun'. It opened as a theatre in 1810, on the little Piazzetta Dino Sarti.

fruits.name: Teatro Arena del Sole
fruits.story: The Arena del Sole means the 'Arena of the Sun'. It opened as a theatre in 1810, on the little Piazzetta Dino Sarti.

fruits.extendedStory: The drawing behind that front is probably Baldassarre Peruzzi's. Look up and you will see a band of stone running right across it. That band was Lazzaro Casario's idea, added in 1584. Then step and look into the courtyard, where Roman stone tablets are set into the wall. They record the baths that Augustus founded here, back when the city was called Bononia.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Entwurf stammt wohl von Baldassarre Peruzzi. Schau nach oben: Ein steinernes Band zieht sich quer über die Front. Es geht auf eine Idee von Lazzaro Casario zurück, von 1584. Und schau in den Hof, wo römische Steintafeln in der Mauer sitzen. Sie halten die Thermen fest, die Augustus hier gründete, als die Stadt Bononia hieß.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The drawing behind that front is probably Baldassarre Peruzzi's. Look up and you will see a band of stone running right across it. That band was Lazzaro Casario's idea, added in 1584. Then step and look into the courtyard, where Roman stone tablets are set into the wall. They record the baths that Augustus founded here, back when the city was called Bononia.

localizedStory.de: Geh die Via Saragozza entlang, und du kommst an einem Bau vorbei, dem die Albergati seit etwa 1520 ihren Namen geben.
localizedStory.en: Walk along Via Saragozza and you pass a grand front the Albergati have given their name to since about 1520.

fruits.name: Palazzo Albergati
fruits.story: Walk along Via Saragozza and you pass a grand front the Albergati have given their name to since about 1520.

fruits.extendedStory: The tower stands 61 metres tall, and it went up in the second half of the twelfth century. The family it is named for, the Azzoguidi, appear in Bologna's written records from 1228. Bologna once bristled with towers like this one. About twenty of them are still standing in the old centre.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Der Turm ist 61 Meter hoch und entstand in der zweiten Hälfte des zwölften Jahrhunderts. Die Familie, nach der er heißt, die Azzoguidi, taucht ab 1228 in Bolognas Aufzeichnungen auf. Früher standen in Bologna viele solcher Türme. Etwa zwanzig davon stehen heute noch in der Altstadt.
localizedExtendedStory.en: The tower stands 61 metres tall, and it went up in the second half of the twelfth century. The family it is named for, the Azzoguidi, appear in Bologna's written records from 1228. Bologna once bristled with towers like this one. About twenty of them are still standing in the old centre.

localizedStory.de: Der Torre degli Azzoguidi ragt 61 Meter hoch. Einer von etwa zwanzig Geschlechtertürmen, die Bologna noch hat.
localizedStory.en: The Torre degli Azzoguidi rises 61 metres. One of about twenty family towers Bologna still has standing.

fruits.name: Torre degli Azzoguidi
fruits.story: The Torre degli Azzoguidi rises 61 metres. One of about twenty family towers Bologna still has standing.

fruits.extendedStory: This gate belonged to the third ring of walls that Bologna built around itself. Antonio Paltroni rebuilt it in 1508. For centuries it had walls running away on either side. Those came down in the early 1900s, and the gate was left standing on its own. That is why it stands by itself today, a gate with no wall to guard.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Dieses Tor gehörte zum dritten Mauerring, den Bologna um sich legte. Antonio Paltroni baute es 1508 um. Jahrhundertelang liefen links und rechts von ihm die Stadtmauern weiter. In den frühen 1900er Jahren wurden sie abgetragen, und das Tor blieb allein zurück. Darum steht es heute für sich, ein Tor ohne Mauer.
localizedExtendedStory.en: This gate belonged to the third ring of walls that Bologna built around itself. Antonio Paltroni rebuilt it in 1508. For centuries it had walls running away on either side. Those came down in the early 1900s, and the gate was left standing on its own. That is why it stands by itself today, a gate with no wall to guard.

localizedStory.de: Bolognas westliches Stadttor seit 1250, hin zur Via Emilia. Das war die alte Römerstraße aus der Stadt.
localizedStory.en: Bologna's western gate since 1250, opening onto the Via Emilia. The old Roman road out of town.

fruits.name: Porta San Felice
fruits.story: Bologna's western gate since 1250, opening onto the Via Emilia. The old Roman road out of town.

fruits.extendedStory: Bologna wrapped itself in walls three times over, and this tower belonged to the second ring. The city calls that ring the cerchia del mille, the ring of the thousand. Work on it began in the late twelfth century. A torresotto is a gate-tower set into the wall, watching whoever came through. Stand under it and you are standing in what was once a hole in the wall.

localizedExtendedStory.de: Bologna legte sich dreimal Mauern um, und dieser Turm gehörte zum zweiten Ring. Die Stadt nennt ihn die cerchia del mille, den Ring der Tausend. Begonnen wurde er im späten 12. Jahrhundert. Ein torresotto ist ein Torturm in der Mauer, der jeden sah, der durchkam. Wer heute darunter steht, steht in einer alten Lücke in der Mauer.
localizedExtendedStory.en: Bologna wrapped itself in walls three times over, and this tower belonged to the second ring. The city calls that ring the cerchia del mille, the ring of the thousand. Work on it began in the late twelfth century. A torresotto is a gate-tower set into the wall, watching whoever came through. Stand under it and you are standing in what was once a hole in the wall.

localizedStory.de: Dieses Stadttor steht seit 1150 über der Via Portanova, nur einen kurzen Weg vom Mercato delle Erbe entfernt.
localizedStory.en: This gate-tower has stood over Via Portanova since 1150, a short walk from the Mercato delle Erbe.

fruits.name: Torresotto di Porta Nuova
fruits.story: This gate-tower has stood over Via Portanova since 1150, a short walk from the Mercato delle Erbe.
